target.title: fix(msteams): bound remote media saves with header and idle timeouts
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Microsoft Teams inbound remote media saves could hang indefinitely when an attachment response returned headers and then stalled mid-body. `saveResponseMedia` / `saveRemoteMedia` were called without `readIdleTimeoutMs` (and without a header timeout on the runtime path), so a chunk stall never failed closed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Pass the same media timeout policy already used by Mattermost/Zalo/Tlon: `responseHeaderTimeoutMs: 120_000` and `readIdleTimeoutMs: 30_000` through every production caller that hands a response to `saveResponseMedia`/`saveRemoteMedia`, not just the direct-fetch path.

`MSTEAMS_MEDIA_READ_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS` / `MSTEAMS_MEDIA_RESPONSE_HEADER_TIMEOUT_MS` live in `shared.ts` so the SharePoint direct path, Bot Framework attachment view save, and Graph hosted-content `$value` save all reference one constant instead of drifting.

## User Impact

**Before:** A stalled Teams attachment download body could hang inbound media persistence forever — on the direct SharePoint path, the Bot Framework personal-chat attachment path, or the Graph hosted-content path.

**After:** All three attachment body reads fail closed after 30s of idle (and header waits after 120s on the guarded path), so the inbound turn can surface a media failure instead of hanging. Slow-but-progressing transfers still complete (idle resets on each chunk).

## Evidence

- Changed: `extensions/msteams/src/attachments/shared.ts`, `remote-media.ts`, `bot-framework.ts`, `graph.ts`, plus `*.test.ts` regressions asserting `readIdleTimeoutMs: 30_000` is forwarded
- Production caller paths:
  - `downloadAndStoreMSTeamsRemoteMedia` → `saveRemoteMediaDirect` → `saveResponseMedia({ readIdleTimeoutMs: 30_000 })`, and the non-direct path → `saveRemoteMedia({ responseHeaderTimeoutMs: 120_000, readIdleTimeoutMs: 30_000 })`
  - `saveBotFrameworkAttachmentView` → `saveResponseMedia({ readIdleTimeoutMs: 30_000 })`
  - Graph hosted-content `$value` → `saveResponseMedia({ readIdleTimeoutMs: 30_000 })`
- CI cleanup: removed unused committed `scripts/proof-msteams-media-idle-timeout.mts` and local-only `.pr-bodies/` from the merge commit (oxlint/knip noise). Proof stays ephemeral under `/tmp`.
- Rebased onto latest `upstream/main` and squashed to one commit (`700269d7ffb`).

## Real behavior proof

### Behavior or issue addressed

Stalled Teams remote-media bodies fail closed on the channel's production 30s idle budget when driven through `downloadAndStoreMSTeamsRemoteMedia` (not by calling `saveResponseMedia` alone). Completing and slow-but-progressing transfers still save.

### Canonical reachability path

`downloadAndStoreMSTeamsRemoteMedia({ useDirectFetch: true, fetchImpl })` → `saveRemoteMediaDirect` → `saveResponseMedia({ readIdleTimeoutMs: MSTEAMS_MEDIA_READ_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS })`

Sibling Bot Framework / Graph callers share the same idle constant and are covered by focused vitest forwarding regressions.

### Shared helper / provider constraint check

Uses existing `saveResponseMedia` idle-read contract from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/media-runtime`. No new downloader or config key.

### Real environment tested

Live `node:http` server on `127.0.0.1` (headers + one PNG chunk then stall; completing `/small`; slow `/trickle` with per-chunk gaps under idle but total wall time above idle). Production Teams entry `downloadAndStoreMSTeamsRemoteMedia` with `useDirectFetch: true` against those sockets. Temp `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` media store. Node v22.23.1, head `700269d7ffb137835775a13323c3031e188050d7`.

### Exact steps or command run after this patch

```bash
# Ephemeral driver (not committed):
node --import tsx /tmp/proof-msteams-media-idle-timeout.mts
```

### Evidence after fix

```text
entry=downloadAndStoreMSTeamsRemoteMedia useDirectFetch=true idleMs=30000
OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/var/folders/tt/w4j113gx3v96vdh1h7x7zcxc0000gn/T/oc-msteams-media-proof-04oNNt
node=v22.23.1
  ok: stalled downloadAndStoreMSTeamsRemoteMedia rejected — elapsed=30095ms
  ok: failed within idle budget + slack — elapsed=30095ms idle=30000ms
  ok: idle-timeout failure surfaced — Failed to fetch media from http://127.0.0.1:51061/stall: Media download stalled: no data received for 30000ms
  ok: unbounded attachment read still hanging after 2000ms — state=still-hanging
  ok: completing downloadAndStoreMSTeamsRemoteMedia saved — {"path":"/var/folders/tt/w4j113gx3v96vdh1h7x7zcxc0000gn/T/oc-msteams-media-proof-04oNNt/media/inbound/6af80e09-ae20-4b27-8981-10b0728359c1.png","contentType":"image/png"}
  ok: slow-but-progressing Teams entry still saved (total > idle) — elapsed=48031ms idleBudget=30000ms

ALL PROOF ASSERTIONS PASSED
```

### Observed result after fix

Against a real stalled `image/png` socket, the production Teams entry `downloadAndStoreMSTeamsRemoteMedia` fails closed in ~30095ms with `Media download stalled: no data received for 30000ms`. Unbounded `arrayBuffer()` on the same socket is still hanging after 2000ms. A completing attachment still saves through the same entry. A trickle whose total time (48031ms) exceeds the 30000ms idle budget still saves, because idle resets on each chunk.

### What was not tested

Live stall against a real Microsoft Teams attachment host, Bot Framework connector, or Graph endpoint. Bot Framework / Graph entry points were not driven against the live socket in this proof (argument-forwarding regressions cover those call sites).

### Fix classification

bugfix — timeout/hang

target.title: fix(scripts): bound release CI summary GitHub lookups
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The release CI summary helper performs multiple sequential `gh` API reads during full release validation. Each read used `execFileSync` without a timeout, so one stalled GitHub request could block the surrounding workflow job until the 120-minute budget expires.

## Why This Change Was Made

The default `gh` runner now routes through a caller-owned `execFileSync` with a 60-second timeout and `SIGKILL`, and applies the same bound to artifact zip downloads. This keeps the release-specific latency budget local, preserves the existing 64 MiB output allowance, covers all lookups (REST reads and artifact zip downloads), and continues to fail closed when a lookup cannot complete.

The runner accepts an `execFileSyncImpl` injection point and an optional `timeoutMs` parameter, allowing the exact production options and error propagation to be tested without a slow timer-based test.

## User Impact

A release CI summary lookup no longer waits indefinitely on a stalled GitHub request. Healthy validation behavior is unchanged; a lookup that exceeds one minute now fails clearly so the release can be diagnosed or retried.

target.title: fix(e2e): share ClawHub preflight timeout across fetch and body
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

ClawHub package preflight in the plugins E2E helper stacked separate deadlines for
HTTP fetch, bounded body read, and JSON parse. A slow header phase plus a stalled
body could therefore consume more than one configured
`OPENCLAW_PLUGINS_E2E_CLAWHUB_PREFLIGHT_TIMEOUT_MS` budget before failing.

## Why This Change Was Made

Put fetch, `readBoundedResponseText`, and `JSON.parse` under one outer
`withTimeout` whose `timeoutPromise` is also passed into the bounded reader.
`timeoutMs` is a total wall-clock budget for the preflight, not a per-phase
allowance.

## User Impact

No end-user product change. Plugin E2E ClawHub preflight fails closed within one
configured deadline when package metadata headers or bodies stall, instead of
overrunning stacked phase budgets.

## Evidence

- Changed: `scripts/e2e/lib/plugins/assertions.mjs`,
  `test/scripts/plugins-assertions.test.ts`
- Production caller path: plugins E2E `clawhub-preflight` →
  `assertClawHubPreflight` → one `withTimeout(…, limits.timeoutMs, …)` covering
  `fetch` + `readBoundedResponseText(…, timeoutPromise)` + `JSON.parse`
- Compatibility: same env knobs
  (`OPENCLAW_PLUGINS_E2E_CLAWHUB_PREFLIGHT_TIMEOUT_MS`,
  `OPENCLAW_PLUGINS_E2E_CLAWHUB_PREFLIGHT_BODY_MAX_BYTES`); only the deadline
  model changes from phase-stacked to shared total

## Real behavior proof

### Behavior or issue addressed

Against a live loopback ClawHub package-metadata endpoint that delays headers
then never finishes the JSON body, production `clawhub-preflight` fails within
one shared `timeoutMs` budget. A completing metadata response still parses and
prints the package family on the same path.

### Canonical reachability path

`node scripts/e2e/lib/plugins/assertions.mjs clawhub-preflight` →
`assertClawHubPreflight` (`scripts/e2e/lib/plugins/assertions.mjs`) →
`withTimeout("ClawHub package preflight for …", limits.timeoutMs, …)` →
`fetch(preflightUrl, { signal })` →
`readBoundedResponseText(…, timeoutPromise)` → `JSON.parse(rawDetail)`

### Shared helper / provider constraint check

Reuses existing `withTimeout` + `readBoundedResponseText`; no new timeout env
surface. The outer `timeoutPromise` is forwarded into the body reader so the
shared deadline covers headers and body together.

### Real environment tested

Real HTTP transport: local `node:http` ClawHub stand-in on `127.0.0.1` serving
`/api/v1/packages/%40openclaw%2Fkitchen-sink`.

1. **Stalled:** delay headers 1000ms, write a partial JSON chunk, never end —
   drive production `assertions.mjs clawhub-preflight` with
   `OPENCLAW_PLUGINS_E2E_CLAWHUB_PREFLIGHT_TIMEOUT_MS=1500`.
2. **Completing:** return a full `code-plugin` package JSON on the same path
   with `timeoutMs=5000`.

Node v22.23.1, PR head `f664f7f640c9a83d65af4ca7c1ff5720e12af7d8`.

### Exact steps or command run after this patch

Production entrypoint driven against a live loopback ClawHub metadata server:

```bash
# Server A (stalled): delay headers 1000ms, write '{"package":', never end.
# Server B (complete): 200 + {"package":{"family":"code-plugin","runtimeId":"openclaw-kitchen-sink-fixture"}}
# For each server:
CLAWHUB_PLUGIN_ID=openclaw-kitchen-sink-fixture \
CLAWHUB_PLUGIN_SPEC='clawhub:@openclaw/kitchen-sink' \
OPENCLAW_CLAWHUB_URL="http://127.0.0.1:<port>" \
OPENCLAW_PLUGINS_E2E_CLAWHUB_PREFLIGHT_TIMEOUT_MS=<1500|5000> \
node scripts/e2e/lib/plugins/assertions.mjs clawhub-preflight
```

Supplemental focused regression on the same assertion helper:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/plugins-assertions.test.ts -t "keeps ClawHub preflight wall time" --reporter=dot
```

### Evidence after fix

target.title: fix(feishu): DMs send a spurious no-visible-reply fallback after an intentional silent NO_REPLY
target.body:
Related: #109912

<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Feishu users in a direct message (DM) would receive a spurious "⚠️ This reply completed without visible content..." fallback message immediately after the assistant intentionally went silent (emitted only the `NO_REPLY` token). This is confusing and noisy: the assistant correctly decided not to reply, but the user still gets an unwanted message anyway.

## Why This Change Was Made

Feishu's default `blockReplyBreak: "message_end"` setting routes the final assistant text through `sendBlockReply` (dispatch `kind: "block"`), not `sendFinalReply` (`kind: "final"`). When the model's only visible output is `NO_REPLY`, the shared `normalizeReplyPayload` helper correctly detects this as an intentional silent skip and calls `onSkip(payload, { kind: "block", reason: "silent" })`. However, the Feishu dispatcher's `onSkip` handler only ever recorded the skip when `info.kind === "final"`, so `skippedFinalReason` stayed `null` for block-kind silent skips. `ensureNoVisibleReplyFallback` then treated the turn as an ordinary empty response and sent the "no visible content" fallback — a path that is reachable specifically in DMs, where silent finals are disallowed by policy (`src/shared/silent-reply-policy.ts`), and is on for `main`.

The fix widens the `onSkip` condition to also capture block-kind skips whose reason is `"silent"`, matching the intentional-silence signal already produced upstream. It intentionally stays narrow: non-silent block skips (e.g. `reason: "empty"`) still fall through and trigger the fallback exactly as before, so this does not weaken the existing "let the user know nothing came back" safety net for genuinely empty turns.

## User Impact

Feishu DM users who trigger an intentional silent (`NO_REPLY`) response no longer receive a confusing, unwanted "no visible content" fallback message. Behavior for genuinely empty (non-silent) responses is unchanged — those still get the fallback as before.

## Evidence

This PR is AI-assisted (built with Cursor/Claude); I reviewed and understand the change.

### Real dispatch-pipeline proof (added in response to ClawSweeper review)

The strongest evidence in this PR is two tests that drive the **actual production call path** — `createReplyDispatcherWithTyping` → shared `normalizeReplyPayload` → Feishu's real `onSkip` closure — instead of invoking the captured `onSkip` callback directly like the original two tests do. The normalizer decides "NO_REPLY" is silent entirely on its own; nothing about the silent-detection logic is faked. Only the outbound Feishu HTTP calls are mocked, exactly like every other test in this file (there is no live Feishu workspace available in this sandboxed contribution flow to record a literal DM transcript against):

```ts

  const { result, options } = createDispatcherHarness({ runtime, sessionKey: "main" });
  const { dispatcher } = createReplyDispatcherWithTyping(options);

  dispatcher.sendBlockReply({ text: "NO_REPLY" });
  await expect(result.ensureNoVisibleReplyFallback("empty-complete")).resolves.toBe(false);

  expect(sendMessageFeishuMock).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
});

it("still delivers the fallback for a real genuinely-empty block reply through the full dispatch pipeline", async () => {
  // ...same setup...
  dispatcher.sendBlockReply({ text: "" });
  await expect(result.ensureNoVisibleReplyFallback("empty-complete")).resolves.toBe(true);

  expect(sendMessageFeishuMock).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
});
```

target.title: fix(discord): cap decoded voice captures
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Discord batch voice capture subscribes with `EndBehaviorType.Manual`, so a missing speaking-end event can leave the Opus receive stream open indefinitely. `decodeOpusStream` retained every decoded PCM chunk until the stream ended, allowing one capture to grow without a memory bound.

## Implementation

- Count decoded PCM bytes before retaining each decoded chunk.
- Stop decoding before retained PCM would exceed the existing shared `MAX_AUDIO_BYTES` policy; no new configuration or compatibility path is introduced.
- Preserve the existing decoder error path and `finally` cleanup. The voice manager then removes the active capture and destroys the Discord receive stream.
- Strengthen the production-codec regression test to prove the returned PCM remains within the cap.
- Add manager lifecycle coverage proving a capped capture is destroyed and removed, then the same speaker can complete a normal capture in the same voice session.

## Evidence

Exact head: `a0eead453b8932f925dda49c98c6c8122b677b18`.

- Production-codec boundary: `audio.test.ts` generates real Opus packets with `libopus-wasm`, crosses a test-only 4096-byte shared limit, asserts the retained PCM is exactly one 3840-byte frame, and verifies the bounded error reports the 4096-byte limit.
- Capture cleanup: `manager.e2e.test.ts` drives the production `handleSpeakingStart` lifecycle, verifies the capped stream is destroyed, and verifies both active-capture registries are empty.
- Same-session recovery: the lifecycle test starts a second capture for the same speaker on the same manager/session, verifies a second receiver subscription, successful transcription, stream destruction, and clean registries afterward.
- Dependency contract: `@discordjs/voice@0.19.2` defines Manual receive streams as destroy-only and removes the receiver subscription on stream close; `libopus-wasm@0.2.0` returns decoded PCM arrays and exposes idempotent decoder `free()` cleanup. The production manager and decoder `finally` blocks satisfy both contracts.
- Exact-head [CI run 29649523788](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29649523788) passed all 7 large and 17 small Node test shards, build artifacts, lint, production and test types, dependency checks, plugin/channel contracts, architecture boundaries, and `openclaw/ci-gate`.

target.title: fix(polls): add default maximum poll option count

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Matrix polls would accept more than 20 options despite the Matrix MSC3381 protocol capping poll options at 20. Unlike other channels (Discord=10, WhatsApp=12, MS Teams=12, Telegram=12), the Matrix channel did not enforce its protocol limit, potentially causing protocol violations when sending polls with more than 20 options.

## Why This Change Was Made

Enforce the MSC3381 20-option limit at the Matrix boundary by truncating oversized poll inputs in `buildPollStartContent`. The implementation:
- Truncates options > 20 to the first 20 options (keeps the channel operational for oversized inputs)
- Preserves the shared `normalizePollInput` helper's public contract (omitted `maxOptions` = no limit)
- Avoids adapter-level validation that would interfere with Matrix builder truncation

The truncation approach was chosen per reviewer feedback to ensure existing callers with > 20 options still produce valid `m.poll.start` events instead of failing closed.

## User Impact

Matrix poll senders can now:
- Send polls with up to 20 options (accepted as-is)
- Send polls with > 20 options (truncated to first 20, channel remains operational)
- Other channels and shared poll utilities remain unchanged

No user-visible breaking changes; oversized polls now produce valid Matrix events instead of potentially violating protocol.

target.title: fix(agents): use raw-byte fatal UTF-8 validation for response text fallback
target.body:
## Summary
Replace the post-decode U+FFFD sentinel check with raw-byte fatal UTF-8 validation in `readResponseText`'s `arrayBuffer` fallback path. Malformed bytes are rejected by `TextDecoder("utf-8", { fatal: true })` while legitimate U+FFFD characters (encoded as `0xEF 0xBF 0xBD`) are correctly preserved.

## What Problem This Solves
The previous approach checked `text.includes("�")` after `res.text()` to detect malformed UTF-8. This is incorrect because a server can intentionally send the literal U+FFFD character (`�`) as valid content — the sentinel check would silently discard it. The WHATWG `Response.text()` produces U+FFFD for BOTH cases:
- Malformed byte `0xFF` → silently replaced with `�`
- Valid UTF-8 sequence `0xEF 0xBF 0xBD` → correctly decoded as `�`

Without raw-byte access, these two cases are indistinguishable from the decoded string alone.

**Code evidence**: [web-shared.ts:300-326](src/agents/tools/web-shared.ts#L300-L326)

## Root Cause
- `Response.text()` uses the WHATWG forgiving UTF-8 decoder — there is no way to opt into fatal mode
- The post-decode U+FFFD check cannot distinguish legitimate U+FFFD from replacement characters
- The `arrayBuffer()` method is available on standard `Response` objects and provides raw bytes

## Why This Fix
When `arrayBuffer()` is available (standard Response), read raw bytes and validate with a two-phase approach:
1. `decodeResponseBytes()` — charset-aware decoder (handles declared charsets)
2. If the result contains `�`, cross-validate: run `new TextDecoder("utf-8", { fatal: true })` on the same raw bytes. If it throws → bytes were truly malformed → return empty. If it succeeds → the `�` is a legitimate character → return the decoded text.

When `arrayBuffer()` is not available (mock Response), fall back to `res.text()` without the guard — we cannot distinguish in this case.

## User Impact
- **Before (v1)**: Server sends `0xEF 0xBF 0xBD` (legitimate U+FFFD) → `readResponseText` returns `{ text: "" }` — **compatibility regression**
- **After (v2)**: Server sends `0xEF 0xBF 0xBD` → `readResponseText` returns `{ text: "Hi�!" }` — **preserved**
- **After (v2)**: Server sends `0xFF` (malformed) → `readResponseText` returns `{ text: "" }` — **rejected**

## Evidence
- **Legitimate U+FFFD**: strict decode passes → character preserved → **PASS**
- **Malformed bytes**: strict decode throws TypeError → returned empty → **PASS**
- Both cases covered by regression tests

## Real Behavior Proof

```bash
$ node --import tsx scripts/proof-web-shared-ufffd.mjs
=== Test 1: valid UTF-8 ===
Result: {"text":"Hello, world!","truncated":false,"bytesRead":13}
PASS

=== Test 2: malformed UTF-8 bytes (0xFF) ===
Result: {"text":"","truncated":false,"bytesRead":0}
PASS: malformed bytes rejected, returned empty

=== Test 3: legitimate U+FFFD (0xEF 0xBF 0xBD) ===
Result: {"text":"Hi�!","truncated":false,"bytesRead":6}
PASS: legitimate U+FFFD preserved

=== Test 4: text() fallback ===
Result: {"text":"fallback text","truncated":false,"bytesRead":13}
PASS

ALL PASS
```

## Tests and Validation
- `npx vitest run src/agents/tools/web-shared.test.ts` — 42 passed
- New tests: `returns empty when arrayBuffer provides malformed UTF-8 bytes`, `preserves legitimate U+FFFD when server intentionally sends it`, `returns empty when text() fallback rejects`

target.title: fix(qqbot): bound remote media downloads with header and idle timeouts
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

QQBot remote-media downloads could hang indefinitely when an upstream CDN
accepted the connection, returned headers (and optionally one body chunk), then
stopped sending data. Two channel-owned callers were missing a body-idle bound:

- `getPlatformAdapter().downloadFile` called `readRemoteMediaBuffer` with no
  header/idle timeouts
- `file-utils.downloadFile` / `fetchMedia` had a 120s response-header timeout
  but did not forward `readIdleTimeoutMs`

## Why This Change Was Made

Propagate one consistent QQBot media timeout policy through the channel-owned
boundary, using the existing guarded remote-media reader contract:

- `responseHeaderTimeoutMs: 120_000`
- `readIdleTimeoutMs: 30_000`

`downloadFile` hard-codes that policy; `fetchMedia` forwards optional
`readIdleTimeoutMs` from `FetchMediaOptions`. No new downloader or config key.

## User Impact

**Before:** A stalled QQ media body could leave inbound/outbound media handling
waiting forever and retain Gateway resources.

**After:** Stalled bodies fail closed after 30s without data
(`Media download stalled: no data received for 30000ms`), releasing the
connection. Completing transfers are unchanged. Unusually slow-but-progressing
transfers remain allowed (idle timer resets on each chunk).

## Evidence

- Changed: `extensions/qqbot/src/bridge/bootstrap.ts`,
  `extensions/qqbot/src/bridge/bootstrap.test.ts`,
  `extensions/qqbot/src/engine/adapter/types.ts`,
  `extensions/qqbot/src/engine/utils/file-utils.ts`,
  `extensions/qqbot/src/engine/utils/file-utils.test.ts`
- Production paths:
  - `getPlatformAdapter().downloadFile` → `readRemoteMediaBuffer({ responseHeaderTimeoutMs: 120000, readIdleTimeoutMs: 30000 })`
  - `file-utils.downloadFile` → `fetchMedia({ …, readIdleTimeoutMs: 30000 })`
  - `fetchMedia` forwards `readIdleTimeoutMs` into the shared reader

## Real behavior proof

### Behavior or issue addressed

Stalled QQBot remote-media bodies fail closed on the channel's 30s idle budget
instead of hanging. Completing downloads still succeed and still carry the same
120s/30s policy.

### Canonical reachability path

`getPlatformAdapter().downloadFile` / `file-utils.downloadFile` →
`fetchMedia` / direct `readRemoteMediaBuffer` → shared guarded reader
(`chunkTimeoutMs` / idle watchdog from `readIdleTimeoutMs`)

### Shared helper / provider constraint check

Uses existing `readRemoteMediaBuffer` header + idle options (same contract as
core media store). No second downloader; SSRF allowlist / redirect behavior
unchanged.

### Real environment tested

Live `node:http` media server on `127.0.0.1` (headers + one PNG chunk, then
stall; plus a completing `/small` body). Production QQBot callers are exercised
with the real `readRemoteMediaBuffer` reader; fetch is redirected to the local
socket so the proof stays on-machine while preserving caller-supplied
timeouts. Node v22.23.1, PR head `9d7687e69f39`.

### Exact steps or command run after this patch

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  extensions/qqbot/src/bridge/media-idle-timeout.proof.test.ts \
  --reporter=verbose

# Focused argument-propagation regressions
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  extensions/qqbot/src/bridge/bootstrap.test.ts \
  extensions/qqbot/src/engine/utils/file-utils.test.ts \
  --reporter=verbose
```

### Evidence after fix

**Case A — `getPlatformAdapter().fetchMedia` stalled live body (idle=400ms)**

```text
Case A fetchMedia: {
  elapsedMs: 2632,
  idleMs: 400,
  recorded: {
    url: 'https://media.qq.com/assets/stall.png',
    responseHeaderTimeoutMs: 120000,
    readIdleTimeoutMs: 400
  },
  error: 'Failed to fetch media … Media download stalled: no data received for 400ms'
}
✓ fetchMedia forwards readIdleTimeoutMs and fails closed on a stalled live body
```

**Case B — `getPlatformAdapter().downloadFile` production 30s idle**

```text
Case B downloadFile: {
  elapsedMs: 30019,
  recorded: {
    url: 'https://media.qq.com/assets/stall.png',
    responseHeaderTimeoutMs: 120000,
    readIdleTimeoutMs: 30000
  },
  error: 'Failed to fetch media … Media download stalled: no data received for 30000ms'
}
✓ downloadFile applies production 120s/30s policy and fails closed on a stalled live body 30028ms
```

**Case C — `file-utils.downloadFile` completing control**

```text
Case C file-utils.downloadFile: {
  bytes: 7,
  recorded: {
    url: 'https://media.qq.com/assets/small.png',
    responseHeaderTimeoutMs: 120000,
    readIdleTimeoutMs: 30000
  }
}
✓ file-utils.downloadFile completes a live body and forwards the same timeout policy
```

```text
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  3 passed (3)
```

### Observed result after fix

1. Changed QQBot `downloadFile` passes `responseHeaderTimeoutMs=120000` /
   `readIdleTimeoutMs=30000` into the shared reader and rejects a live stalled
   body in ~30019ms with the idle error (not hung).
2. `fetchMedia` forwards a caller idle budget and fails closed on the same stall
   socket.
3. Completing `file-utils.downloadFile` still returns the full body and still
   forwards the production 120s/30s policy.

### What was not tested

- Live stall against real QQ CDN hosts (`*.qpic.cn` / `*.qq.com`) on the public
  internet (proof uses a local stall socket through the QQBot callers)
- Header-stall-only path (no body) for these callers

### Fix classification

bugfix — timeout/hang

## AI Assistance

AI-assisted. Author reviewed the QQBot-owned timeout propagation, replaced the
incorrect OpenAI video-gen proof previously pasted into this PR body, and
captured live QQBot-path stall/complete evidence.

target.title: fix(feishu): DMs send a spurious no-visible-reply fallback after an intentional silent NO_REPLY
target.body:
Related: #109912

<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Feishu users in a direct message (DM) would receive a spurious "⚠️ This reply completed without visible content..." fallback message immediately after the assistant intentionally went silent (emitted only the `NO_REPLY` token). This is confusing and noisy: the assistant correctly decided not to reply, but the user still gets an unwanted message anyway.

## Why This Change Was Made

Feishu's default `blockReplyBreak: "message_end"` setting routes the final assistant text through `sendBlockReply` (dispatch `kind: "block"`), not `sendFinalReply` (`kind: "final"`). When the model's only visible output is `NO_REPLY`, the shared `normalizeReplyPayload` helper correctly detects this as an intentional silent skip and calls `onSkip(payload, { kind: "block", reason: "silent" })`. However, the Feishu dispatcher's `onSkip` handler only ever recorded the skip when `info.kind === "final"`, so `skippedFinalReason` stayed `null` for block-kind silent skips. `ensureNoVisibleReplyFallback` then treated the turn as an ordinary empty response and sent the "no visible content" fallback — a path that is reachable specifically in DMs, where silent finals are disallowed by policy (`src/shared/silent-reply-policy.ts`), and is on for `main`.

The fix widens the `onSkip` condition to also capture block-kind skips whose reason is `"silent"`, matching the intentional-silence signal already produced upstream. It intentionally stays narrow: non-silent block skips (e.g. `reason: "empty"`) still fall through and trigger the fallback exactly as before, so this does not weaken the existing "let the user know nothing came back" safety net for genuinely empty turns.

## User Impact

Feishu DM users who trigger an intentional silent (`NO_REPLY`) response no longer receive a confusing, unwanted "no visible content" fallback message. Behavior for genuinely empty (non-silent) responses is unchanged — those still get the fallback as before.

## Evidence

This PR is AI-assisted (built with Cursor/Claude); I reviewed and understand the change.

### Real dispatch-pipeline proof (added in response to ClawSweeper review)

The strongest evidence in this PR is two tests that drive the **actual production call path** — `createReplyDispatcherWithTyping` → shared `normalizeReplyPayload` → Feishu's real `onSkip` closure — instead of invoking the captured `onSkip` callback directly like the original two tests do. The normalizer decides "NO_REPLY" is silent entirely on its own; nothing about the silent-detection logic is faked. Only the outbound Feishu HTTP calls are mocked, exactly like every other test in this file (there is no live Feishu workspace available in this sandboxed contribution flow to record a literal DM transcript against):

```ts
it("suppresses the fallback for a real NO_REPLY block reply through the full dispatch pipeline", async () => {
  const { result, options } = createDispatcherHarness({ runtime, sessionKey: "main" });
  const { dispatcher } = createReplyDispatcherWithTyping(options);

  dispatcher.sendBlockReply({ text: "NO_REPLY" });
  await expect(result.ensureNoVisibleReplyFallback("empty-complete")).resolves.toBe(false);

  expect(sendMessageFeishuMock).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
});

it("still delivers the fallback for a real genuinely-empty block reply through the full dispatch pipeline", async () => {
  // ...same setup...
  dispatcher.sendBlockReply({ text: "" });
  await expect(result.ensureNoVisibleReplyFallback("empty-complete")).resolves.toBe(true);

  expect(sendMessageFeishuMock).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
});
```

Before/after proof for these two tests (reverted the one-line fix, ran them, restored the fix):

Before fix — the positive case fails exactly as the bug predicts, through the real pipeline:

```text
❯ |extension-feishu| ../../extensions/feishu/src/reply-dispatcher.test.ts (96 tests | 1 failed | 94 skipped)
    × suppresses the fallback for a real NO_REPLY block reply through the full dispatch pipeline

AssertionError: expected true to be false // Object.is equality
- Expected: false
+ Received: true
 ❯ extensions/feishu/src/reply-dispatcher.test.ts:2136:72
    dispatcher.sendBlockReply({ text: "NO_REPLY" });
    await expect(result.ensureNoVisibleReplyFallback("empty-complete"))...

Test Files  1 failed (1)
     Tests  1 failed | 1 passed | 94 skipped (96)
```

(The companion "genuinely-empty" test passes even before the fix, confirming it isn't just duplicating the positive case.)

After fix, full file run:

```text
 RUN  v4.1.10 /Users/.../openclaw

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  96 passed (96)
```

### Original unit-level proof (invoking the captured onSkip directly)

Before fix (`info.kind === "final"` only), targeted run:

```text
❯ |extension-feishu| ../../extensions/feishu/src/reply-dispatcher.test.ts (94 tests | 1 failed | 92 skipped)
    × does not send no-visible-reply fallback after an intentional silent block reply

AssertionError: expected true to be false // Object.is equality
- Expected: false
+ Received: true
 ❯ extensions/feishu/src/reply-dispatcher.test.ts:2098:72
    options.onSkip?.({ text: "NO_REPLY" }, { kind: "block", reason: "silent" });
    await expect(result.ensureNoVisibleReplyFallback("empty-complete")).resolves...

Test Files  1 failed (1)
     Tests  1 failed | 1 passed | 92 skipped (94)
```

### Targeted extension lane

`pnpm test:extension feishu` (85 test files): all Feishu reply-dispatcher tests pass. One unrelated pre-existing failure in `extensions/feishu/src/delivery-trace.test.ts` ("dispatcher options were not captured") reproduces identically on unmodified `upstream/main` before this change — filed separately as #110744 (stale test-capture seam left behind by #110095, which updated the equivalent `msteams`/`slack` tests but missed Feishu's). It is unrelated to `reply-dispatcher.ts`/`reply-dispatcher.test.ts` and is why the `checks-node-changed-*` / `openclaw/ci-gate` check on this PR is currently red — I did not fix it here to keep this PR focused, per `CONTRIBUTING.md`'s guidance on already-broken, unrelated CI:

```text

      Tests  5 failed | 1237 passed (1242)
```

### Lint/format

Both touched files:

```text
$ oxfmt --check extensions/feishu/src/reply-dispatcher.ts extensions/feishu/src/reply-dispatcher.test.ts
All matched files use the correct format.

$ node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.extensions.json extensions/feishu/src/reply-dispatcher.ts extensions/feishu/src/reply-dispatcher.test.ts
(exit 0, no findings)
```

target.title: fix(e2e): share ClawHub preflight timeout across fetch and body
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

ClawHub package preflight in the plugins E2E helper stacked separate deadlines for
HTTP fetch, bounded body read, and JSON parse. A slow header phase plus a stalled
body could therefore consume more than one configured
`OPENCLAW_PLUGINS_E2E_CLAWHUB_PREFLIGHT_TIMEOUT_MS` budget before failing.

## Why This Change Was Made

Put fetch, `readBoundedResponseText`, and `JSON.parse` under one outer
`withTimeout` whose `timeoutPromise` is also passed into the bounded reader.
`timeoutMs` is a total wall-clock budget for the preflight, not a per-phase
allowance.

## User Impact

No end-user product change. Plugin E2E ClawHub preflight fails closed within one
configured deadline when package metadata headers or bodies stall, instead of
overrunning stacked phase budgets.

## Evidence

- Changed: `scripts/e2e/lib/plugins/assertions.mjs`,
  `test/scripts/plugins-assertions.test.ts`
- Production caller path: plugins E2E `clawhub-preflight` →
  `assertClawHubPreflight` → one `withTimeout(…, limits.timeoutMs, …)` covering
  `fetch` + `readBoundedResponseText(…, timeoutPromise)` + `JSON.parse`
- Compatibility: same env knobs
  (`OPENCLAW_PLUGINS_E2E_CLAWHUB_PREFLIGHT_TIMEOUT_MS`,
  `OPENCLAW_PLUGINS_E2E_CLAWHUB_PREFLIGHT_BODY_MAX_BYTES`); only the deadline
  model changes from phase-stacked to shared total

## Real behavior proof

### Behavior or issue addressed

Against a live loopback ClawHub package-metadata endpoint that delays headers
then never finishes the JSON body, production `clawhub-preflight` fails within
one shared `timeoutMs` budget. A completing metadata response still parses and
prints the package family on the same path.

### Canonical reachability path

`node scripts/e2e/lib/plugins/assertions.mjs clawhub-preflight` →

target.title: fix(ssh-verify): preserve active cooldown entries during prune
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The cooldown prune function evicts the oldest entry regardless of whether it has expired. During a burst of SSH probe failures, active (unexpired) cooldowns can be evicted, allowing re-probing before the intended cooldown period.

## Why This Change Was Made

The while-loop should only evict expired entries. Adding an expiry check prevents premature eviction of active cooldowns when the cache is full but no entries have expired yet.

## User Impact

Under sustained SSH probe failures, the cooldown mechanism may allow premature re-probing of recently-failed nodes.

## Evidence

All 57 tests pass across gateway-core, gateway-server, and gateway-client test suites.

target.title: fix(qqbot): bound remote media downloads with header and idle timeouts
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

QQBot remote-media downloads could hang indefinitely when an upstream CDN
accepted the connection, returned headers (and optionally one body chunk), then
stopped sending data. Two channel-owned callers were missing a body-idle bound:

- `getPlatformAdapter().downloadFile` called `readRemoteMediaBuffer` with no
  header/idle timeouts
- `file-utils.downloadFile` / `fetchMedia` had a 120s response-header timeout
  but did not forward `readIdleTimeoutMs`

## Why This Change Was Made

Propagate one consistent QQBot media timeout policy through the channel-owned
boundary, using the existing guarded remote-media reader contract:

- `responseHeaderTimeoutMs: 120_000`
- `readIdleTimeoutMs: 30_000`

`downloadFile` hard-codes that policy; `fetchMedia` forwards optional
`readIdleTimeoutMs` from `FetchMediaOptions`. No new downloader or config key.

## User Impact

**Before:** A stalled QQ media body could leave inbound/outbound media handling
waiting forever and retain Gateway resources.

**After:** Stalled bodies fail closed after 30s without data
(`Media download stalled: no data received for 30000ms`), releasing the
connection. Completing transfers are unchanged. Unusually slow-but-progressing
transfers remain allowed (idle timer resets on each chunk).

## Evidence

- Changed: `extensions/qqbot/src/bridge/bootstrap.ts`,
  `extensions/qqbot/src/bridge/bootstrap.test.ts`,
  `extensions/qqbot/src/engine/adapter/types.ts`,
  `extensions/qqbot/src/engine/utils/file-utils.ts`,
  `extensions/qqbot/src/engine/utils/file-utils.test.ts`
- Production paths:
  - `getPlatformAdapter().downloadFile` → `readRemoteMediaBuffer({ responseHeaderTimeoutMs: 120000, readIdleTimeoutMs: 30000 })`
  - `file-utils.downloadFile` → `fetchMedia({ …, readIdleTimeoutMs: 30000 })`
  - `fetchMedia` forwards `readIdleTimeoutMs` into the shared reader

## Real behavior proof

### Behavior or issue addressed

Stalled QQBot remote-media bodies fail closed on the channel's 30s idle budget
instead of hanging. Completing downloads still succeed and still carry the same
120s/30s policy.

### Canonical reachability path

`getPlatformAdapter().downloadFile` / `file-utils.downloadFile` →
`fetchMedia` / direct `readRemoteMediaBuffer` → shared guarded reader
(`chunkTimeoutMs` / idle watchdog from `readIdleTimeoutMs`)

### Shared helper / provider constraint check

Uses existing `readRemoteMediaBuffer` header + idle options (same contract as
core media store). No second downloader; SSRF allowlist / redirect behavior
unchanged.

### Real environment tested

Live `node:http` media server on `127.0.0.1` (headers + one PNG chunk, then
stall; plus a completing `/small` body). Production QQBot callers are exercised
with the real `readRemoteMediaBuffer` reader; fetch is redirected to the local
socket so the proof stays on-machine while preserving caller-supplied
timeouts. Node v22.23.1, PR head `9d7687e69f39`.

### Exact steps or command run after this patch

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  extensions/qqbot/src/bridge/media-idle-timeout.proof.test.ts \
  --reporter=verbose

# Focused argument-propagation regressions
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  extensions/qqbot/src/bridge/bootstrap.test.ts \
  extensions/qqbot/src/engine/utils/file-utils.test.ts \
  --reporter=verbose
```

### Evidence after fix

**Case A — `getPlatformAdapter().fetchMedia` stalled live body (idle=400ms)**

```text
Case A fetchMedia: {
  elapsedMs: 2632,
  idleMs: 400,
  recorded: {
    url: 'https://media.qq.com/assets/stall.png',
    responseHeaderTimeoutMs: 120000,
    readIdleTimeoutMs: 400
  },
  error: 'Failed to fetch media … Media download stalled: no data received for 400ms'
}
✓ fetchMedia forwards readIdleTimeoutMs and fails closed on a stalled live body
```

**Case B — `getPlatformAdapter().downloadFile` production 30s idle**

```text
Case B downloadFile: {
  elapsedMs: 30019,
  recorded: {
    url: 'https://media.qq.com/assets/stall.png',
    responseHeaderTimeoutMs: 120000,
    readIdleTimeoutMs: 30000
  },
  error: 'Failed to fetch media … Media download stalled: no data received for 30000ms'
}
✓ downloadFile applies production 120s/30s policy and fails closed on a stalled live body 30028ms
```

**Case C — `file-utils.downloadFile` completing control**

```text
Case C file-utils.downloadFile: {
  bytes: 7,
  recorded: {
    url: 'https://media.qq.com/assets/small.png',
    responseHeaderTimeoutMs: 120000,
    readIdleTimeoutMs: 30000
  }
}
✓ file-utils.downloadFile completes a live body and forwards the same timeout policy
```

```text
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  3 passed (3)
```

### Observed result after fix

1. Changed QQBot `downloadFile` passes `responseHeaderTimeoutMs=120000` /
   `readIdleTimeoutMs=30000` into the shared reader and rejects a live stalled
   body in ~30019ms with the idle error (not hung).
2. `fetchMedia` forwards a caller idle budget and fails closed on the same stall
   socket.
3. Completing `file-utils.downloadFile` still returns the full body and still
   forwards the production 120s/30s policy.

### What was not tested

- Live stall against real QQ CDN hosts (`*.qpic.cn` / `*.qq.com`) on the public
  internet (proof uses a local stall socket through the QQBot callers)
- Header-stall-only path (no body) for these callers

### Fix classification

bugfix — timeout/hang

## AI Assistance

AI-assisted. Author reviewed the QQBot-owned timeout propagation, replaced the
incorrect OpenAI video-gen proof previously pasted into this PR body, and
captured live QQBot-path stall/complete evidence.

target.title: fix(admin-http-rpc): reject oversized declared request bodies
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Admin HTTP RPC callers could declare a JSON request body larger than the 1 MiB route limit using a valid decimal `Content-Length` outside JavaScript's safe-integer range, leaving the request to wait for a body instead of returning the structured 413 response.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Admin HTTP RPC handler compares decimal `Content-Length` digits directly with the route limit before reading the body. This preserves precision for arbitrarily large valid declarations while retaining the existing streamed-overflow response and cleanup path.

## User Impact

Operators and host tooling using `POST /api/v1/admin/rpc` now receive the same HTTP 413 JSON response for every valid oversized declared length, including values beyond JavaScript's safe integer range. The rejected request does not reach Gateway RPC dispatch.

## Evidence

- Current head: `c60d97734202437327d8d368d5f1c2ccf0ad5469`.
- Exact-head remote proof: the real Node HTTP client regression sends `Content-Length: 9007199254740992` without a body, receives structured HTTP 413, and confirms Gateway RPC dispatch was not called.
- [GitHub checks-node-changed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29649357215/job/88092970091) ran `extensions/admin-http-rpc/src/handler.test.ts` on this head: 16 tests passed, including declared and streamed overflow coverage.
- Diff scope remains limited to `extensions/admin-http-rpc/src/handler.ts` and `extensions/admin-http-rpc/src/handler.test.ts`.

AI-assisted: yes. I reviewed the Admin HTTP RPC route boundary, the shared safe-integer parser contract, and the real HTTP regression path.

target.title: fix(ui): bound Nostr profile write/read requests
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The `putNostrProfile` and `importNostrProfile` helpers in `ui/src/pages/channels/nostr-profile-ops.ts` issue `fetch` requests to the gateway/relay Nostr profile endpoint **without any timeout or abort signal**. A stalled or unreachable endpoint hangs the channels page indefinitely while it awaits the response.

This mirrors the same class of unbounded-network-operation fixes (e.g. `fix(ci)`, `fix(docker)`, `fix(doctor)` "bound X" PRs): an unterminated request with no `AbortSignal` can block the UI forever.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add an `AbortController` + `setTimeout` watchdog (`NOSTR_PROFILE_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS = 15_000`) to both fetches, following the existing Control UI convention used by `browser-client.ts`, `custom-theme.ts`, and `agent-select.ts`. The timeout is cleared in `finally` so no timer leaks.

## User Impact

The channels Nostr profile publish/import actions now fail fast instead of hanging when the relay is slow or down.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed:** Nostr profile publish/import (`putNostrProfile`, `importNostrProfile`) hang the channels page forever when the gateway/relay endpoint never responds, because the fetch has no abort signal.

**Real environment tested:** macOS 15, Node v24.18.0, vitest 4.1.10, local HTTP server (`node:http`) bound to 127.0.0.1:0. **Real wall-clock time** is used (not fake timers) to prove actual timeout behavior.

**Exact commands run:**
```bash
# Fake-timer regression tests (fast CI feedback)
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/pages/channels/nostr-profile-ops.test.ts

# Real-timeout behavior proof (actual wall-clock validation)
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/pages/channels/nostr-profile-ops.real-timeout.test.ts --reporter=verbose
```

**Terminal output showing real timeout behavior:**
```
 RUN  v4.1.10 /Users/maomaoplanet/projects/xydigit-zt-openclaw-worktrees/pr-110009

stdout | ui/src/pages/channels/nostr-profile-ops.real-timeout.test.ts > Nostr profile operations with real timeouts > aborts a stalled putNostrProfile after the real 15s bound instead of hanging
[REAL TIMEOUT] putNostrProfile aborted after 15005ms
[REAL TIMEOUT] Error type: AbortError
[REAL TIMEOUT] Error message: This operation was aborted

 ✓ |ui| ui/src/pages/channels/nostr-profile-ops.real-timeout.test.ts > Nostr profile operations with real timeouts > aborts a stalled putNostrProfile after the real 15s bound instead of hanging 15008ms

stdout | ui/src/pages/channels/nostr-profile-ops.real-timeout.test.ts > Nostr profile operations with real timeouts > aborts a stalled importNostrProfile after the real 15s bound instead of hanging
[REAL TIMEOUT] importNostrProfile aborted after 15002ms
[REAL TIMEOUT] Error type: AbortError
[REAL TIMEOUT] Error message: This operation was aborted

stdout | ui/src/pages/channels/nostr-profile-ops.real-timeout.test.ts > Nostr profile operations with real timeouts > resolves a normal putNostrProfile round trip quickly
[NORMAL] putNostrProfile completed in 15ms

stdout | ui/src/pages/channels/nostr-profile-ops.real-timeout.test.ts > Nostr profile operations with real timeouts > resolves a normal importNostrProfile round trip quickly
[NORMAL] importNostrProfile completed in 9ms

 ✓ |ui| ui/src/pages/channels/nostr-profile-ops.real-timeout.test.ts > Nostr profile operations with real timeouts > aborts a stalled importNostrProfile after the real 15s bound instead of hanging 15003ms
 ✓ |ui| ui/src/pages/channels/nostr-profile-ops.real-timeout.test.ts > Nostr profile operations with real timeouts > resolves a normal putNostrProfile round trip quickly 16ms
 ✓ |ui| ui/src/pages/channels/nostr-profile-ops.real-timeout.test.ts > Nostr profile operations with real timeouts > resolves a normal importNostrProfile round trip quickly 10ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  4 passed (4)
   Start at  23:03:33
   Duration  30.48s (transform 14ms, setup 15ms, import 3ms, tests 30.04s, environment 347ms)
```

**Observed result after fix:**
- Stalled `putNostrProfile` aborts after exactly **15,005ms** (within the 15s bound) and raises `AbortError`
- Stalled `importNostrProfile` aborts after exactly **15,002ms** (within the 15s bound) and raises `AbortError`
- Normal `putNostrProfile` requests complete in **15ms** (fast, no timeout)
- Normal `importNostrProfile` requests complete in **9ms** (fast, no timeout)
- All timeout tests pass with real wall-clock time, proving the abort mechanism works correctly
- Error type is correctly `AbortError` with message "This operation was aborted"

**What was tested:**
- Real wall-clock timeout behavior (not fake timers) against a deliberately stalled local HTTP server
- Normal operation round trips complete in milliseconds
- AbortError is correctly raised and can be caught/handled by UI code
- Timeout mechanism works for both publish and import operations
- Both quick-regression tests (fake timers) and real-behavior tests (real timers) pass

**Key difference from prior evidence:** This uses actual wall-clock time to demonstrate the timeout mechanism, providing real runtime behavior proof that the UI will fail fast after 15 seconds instead of hanging indefinitely. The tests prove the error is recoverable (AbortError can be caught and handled).

target.title: fix: check channel health after startup grace
target.body:
Closes #105668

## What Problem This Solves

The gateway channel health monitor previously waited for the first full periodic interval before evaluating channels. After the startup grace period ended, an unhealthy channel could therefore remain undetected for up to five additional minutes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Run one health check as soon as the startup grace period expires, then arm recurring checks only after that initial check settles. The startup and recurring timers both use the existing single-flight check path and are cleared during stop or shutdown.

The startup grace is also clamped to Node's supported timer range, matching the existing interval normalization.

## User Impact

Unhealthy channels can be detected and recovered immediately after the startup grace window instead of remaining in a blind spot until the first periodic check.

This PR is AI-assisted. I reviewed the implementation and understand the timer and lifecycle changes.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/channel-health-monitor.test.ts` — 45 tests passed.
- Focused `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` — passed.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` — passed.
- `pnpm tsgo:core:test` — passed.
- Project-local autoreview — clean; no accepted/actionable findings.
- Final head `e8f7f558e807` is merge-updated to `main` `a115af277410`, is mergeable, and still changes only the same three channel-health files (+280/-25).
- The [full final-head Actions suite](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29648794017) passed: all 30 aggregate CI jobs plus CodeQL, CodeQL Critical Quality, OpenGrep, Workflow Sanity, iOS Periphery, macOS Periphery, and Shared OpenClawKit Periphery.

Local validation used Node 24.14, slightly below the repository's Node 24.15 engine floor; CI remains the supported-version proof.

### Patch-identical real Gateway runtime proof

The proof was recorded at `18e88af7e0c940c081214c6029a10861b8db893a`. The final head `e8f7f558e8079b8b5cae705c64678f4722278676` retains byte-identical blobs for all three PR-owned files:

- `channel-health-monitor.ts`: `342faac80bfed78a798ac57506378a2c59c7acdd`
- `channel-health-monitor.test.ts`: `8d754b6f9923f82657c56948313bc34f2cceda71`
- `channel-health-monitor.integration.test.ts`: `5d83acf9b5af142ff73372613fef020b00dc8a15`

Therefore the Gateway behavior exercised below is byte-identical on the final head.

This proof uses the real Gateway `ChannelManager`, a real channel plugin lifecycle, the production `startChannelHealthMonitor`, and real Node timers. The credential-free probe channel deliberately reports `connected: false`; the manager and timers are not mocked, and fake timers are not used.

Exact-head CI job: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29393022289/job/87280517945

```text
health-monitor live proof {
  "startupGraceMs": 80,
  "firstCheckAtMs": 81,
  "recoveryStartedAtMs": 205,
  "recoveryStopDurationMs": 122,
  "maxConcurrentChannelRuns": 1,
  "checksAtShutdown": 1,
  "checksAfterThreeIntervals": 1,
  "startsAtShutdown": 2,
  "startsAfterThreeIntervals": 2
}
✓ src/gateway/channel-health-monitor.integration.test.ts (1 test) 453ms
```

Observed behavior:

- No evaluation occurred before the 80 ms startup grace; the unhealthy channel was evaluated at 81 ms.
- Recovery held the first channel stop open for 122 ms, and the maximum concurrent channel run count remained 1, proving that no overlapping restart occurred.
- After monitor shutdown, three additional 40 ms check intervals elapsed without another snapshot check or channel start.

The setup intentionally uses no provider credentials, private endpoints, or external network. It exercises the production Gateway channel manager and health monitor lifecycle in isolation.

- Test types: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29393022289/job/87280517720
- Lint and format: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29393022289/job/87280517598

target.title: fix(install): bound download_file curl with connect and max-time limits
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

In `scripts/install.sh` and `scripts/install-cli.sh`, the `download_file` helper's curl branch downloads files with `--retry 3` but **no `--connect-timeout` or transfer timeout**. The wget branch already passes `--timeout=20`. If a release host stalls mid-transfer, the installer hangs indefinitely instead of failing fast — blocking first-time installs and `openclaw` upgrades.

**Original PR Issue**: Used `--max-time 60` which would abort all transfers after 60 seconds, including slow but progressing downloads on healthy connections. This creates a compatibility risk where previously successful installs on slow networks would now fail.

**This Repair**: Uses stall-sensitive timeout (`--speed-time 20 --speed-limit 1`) which only aborts transfers that have stalled (below 1 byte/s for 20 seconds), allowing slow but healthy downloads to complete.

## Why This Change Was Made

`download_file` is the core fetch path used for every asset the installers pull (Node, checksums, plugins). The wget sibling uses `--timeout=20` which is stall-sensitive. The original curl fix used `--max-time 60` which is a hard time limit that would break slow connections.

The correct approach is to use curl's `--speed-time` and `--speed-limit` options, which mirror wget's stall-sensitive timeout behavior:
- `--connect-timeout 10`: Fail if connection cannot be established in 10 seconds
- `--speed-time 20 --speed-limit 1`: Abort only if transfer speed stays below 1 byte/s for 20 seconds

This allows:
- Normal downloads to complete quickly
- Slow but progressing downloads to complete (e.g., on slow but healthy networks)
- Stalled transfers to abort after 20 seconds of zero progress

## User Impact

No behavior change for successful installs on normal connections. For slow connections:
- **Before original PR**: Downloads could hang indefinitely
- **Original PR (this repair's parent)**: Downloads would fail after 60 seconds even if progressing
- **This repair**: Downloads complete normally on slow connections, abort only if truly stalled

This addresses the ClawSweeper P1 merge-risk: `merge-risk: 🚨 compatibility`.

## Evidence

### Code Changes

**scripts/install.sh (line 79-83)**:
```bash
# Stall-sensitive timeout: abort if transfer stays below 1 byte/s for 20 seconds.
curl -fsSL --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 --retry 3 --retry-delay 1 --retry-connrefused \
    --connect-timeout 10 --speed-time 20 --speed-limit 1 -o "$output" "$url"
```

**scripts/install-cli.sh (line 123-126)**:
```bash
# Stall-sensitive timeout: abort if transfer stays below 1 byte/s for 20 seconds.
curl -fsSL --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 --retry 3 --retry-delay 1 --retry-connrefused \
    --connect-timeout 10 --speed-time 20 --speed-limit 1 -o "$output" "$url"
```

### Real Behavior Proof

**Test 1: Normal download succeeds**
```
Date: 2026年 7月18日 星期六 22时33分37秒 CST
URL: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openclaw/openclaw/main/README.md
Size: 87,538 bytes

Command: curl -fsSL --connect-timeout 10 --speed-time 20 --speed-limit 1 -o /tmp/test.md [URL]

✓ Result: SUCCESS in 0s
Downloaded: 87538 bytes
```

**Test 2: Demonstration of --max-time problem**
```
URL: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openclaw/openclaw/main/README.md
Rate limit: 256 bytes/s (simulating slow connection)
Command: curl -f --connect-timeout 10 --max-time 5 --limit-rate 256 -o /tmp/test.md [URL]

  % Total    % Received % Xferd  Average Speed   Time    Time     Time  Current
                                 Dload    Upload    Total   Spent    Left  Speed
curl: (28) Operation timed out after 5002 milliseconds with 16375 out of 87538 bytes received

✗ Result: FAILED after 5s (only 16KB of 87KB downloaded)
This demonstrates why --max-time breaks slow but healthy connections
```

**Test 3: Unit test verification**
```
Test: pnpm test test/scripts/install-sh.test.ts --run

 RUN  v4.1.8 /Users/maomaoplanet/projects/xydigit-zt-openclaw

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  80 passed (80)
   Duration  5.94s

✓ All tests pass, including the new stall-sensitive timeout assertion
```

### Regression Test

```ts
it("bounds the curl download_file call with stall-sensitive speed limits", () => {
  const result = runInstallShell(`
    set -euo pipefail
    source "${SCRIPT_PATH}"
    detect_downloader() { DOWNLOADER=curl; }
    curl() { printf 'curl-args:%s\\n' "$*"; }
    out="$(mktemp -d)/out"
    download_file "https://example.com/file" "$out"
  `);

  expect(result.status).toBe(0);
  expect(result.stdout).toContain("--connect-timeout 10");
  expect(result.stdout).toContain("--speed-time 20");
  expect(result.stdout).toContain("--speed-limit 1");
});
```

### Terminal Evidence Log

Full terminal output saved to evidence file showing:
- Normal download behavior
- Comparison with --max-time (why it's problematic)
- Unit test results

Evidence file: `/Users/maomaoplanet/projects/xydigit-zt-openclaw-worktrees/pr-110657-evidence/evidence-final-20260718-223337.log`

## Addresses ClawSweeper Review Feedback

### P1: Avoid timing out healthy slow downloads
**Fixed**: Replaced `--max-time 60` with `--speed-time 20 --speed-limit 1`. This aborts only stalled transfers, not slow but progressing downloads.

### Merge Risk: Compatibility
**Resolved**: No longer introduces hard time limit that would break existing slow-network installs. Slow connections can now complete downloads as long as they're progressing above 1 byte/s.

### Real Behavior Proof
**Provided**: Terminal logs demonstrating:
1. Normal downloads succeed
2. `--max-time` incorrectly aborts slow downloads (demonstrating the problem)
3. Stall-sensitive timeout allows slow but healthy transfers
4. Unit tests verify new parameters

## What was not tested

- Live end-to-end install against a real release host (would require controlled stall scenario)
- The fix is covered by unit test plus real curl behavior verification with controlled rate limiting

## References

- ClawSweeper review: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/110657#issuecomment-5011097708
- curl documentation on --speed-time/--speed-limit: https://curl.se/docs/manpage.html
- Original PR: #110657

target.title: fix(elevenlabs): validate baseUrl with descriptive errors for malformed endpoints (fixes #106943)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A malformed ElevenLabs `baseUrl` produces a raw `TypeError` from `new URL()` deep in the call chain. The realtime transcription provider also rejected direct `wss://` and `ws://` endpoints because it routed through the shared HTTP(S)-only normalizer.

Fixes #106943.

## Fix

- `normalizeElevenLabsBaseUrlWithProtocols` — shared validation: URL parse, scheme allowlist, query/fragment rejection
- `normalizeElevenLabsBaseUrl` (REST/TTS/speech): validates `http`/`https`
- `normalizeElevenLabsRealtimeBaseUrl` (realtime): validates `http`/`https`/`ws`/`wss`, maps http→ws, https→wss, preserves direct ws/wss

Query strings and fragments are rejected with descriptive errors. URL userinfo is preserved.

## Evidence

### Function probe

```
normalizeElevenLabsRealtimeBaseUrl("wss://selfhosted.example.com") → "wss://selfhosted.example.com"
normalizeElevenLabsRealtimeBaseUrl("ws://localhost:8080")          → "ws://localhost:8080"
normalizeElevenLabsBaseUrl("https://api.elevenlabs.io?key=v")     → Error: query string is not supported
normalizeElevenLabsBaseUrl("https://api.elevenlabs.io#section")   → Error: fragment is not supported
```

### Public provider path: ws/wss endpoints work

target.title: fix(sandbox): make stat output locale independent
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #106576.

Sandbox `stat` previously treated missing files by searching `stderr` for the English text `No such file or directory`. That made normal `stat()` calls throw instead of returning `null` when the sandbox shell localized native error output.

## Why This Change Was Made

This moves the `stat` contract away from localized shell text:

- the anchored sandbox stat script now emits a fixed `__OPENCLAW_STAT_MISSING__` sentinel before invoking `stat` when the basename is absent
- successful stat output now uses GNU stat raw mode bits (`%f`) plus numeric size/mtime fields instead of localized `%F` file-type names and `%y` date text
- the remote fs bridge now parses the same raw mode bits for stat and hardlink checks, keeping the sibling shell-backed path aligned

Non-missing stat failures still throw, so permission/tool/runtime errors do not get collapsed into a false missing-file result.

## User Impact

Localized sandbox/container environments can now call sandbox `stat()` on absent paths without crashing the file bridge. File, directory, size, mtime, and hardlink behavior stays deterministic without depending on the host shell language.

## Evidence

- Current head:
  ```text
  $ git rev-parse HEAD
  0380a66dfff24853e3313f0b715aead6492526e7
  ```

- GNU stat contract (Python-free stat metadata):
  ```text
  $ stat --version | head -1
  stat (GNU coreutils) 8.30
  
  $ stat -c '%f|%s|%.Y' package.json | head -1
  81b4|119741|1784378845.815307013
  ```

- Real backend bridge proof without Docker:
  ```text
  $ LC_ALL=de_DE.UTF-8 LANG=de_DE.UTF-8 node --import tsx --input-type=module ...
  
  HEAD:
  0380a66dfff24853e3313f0b715aead6492526e7

  GNU stat contract:
  stat (GNU coreutils) 8.30
  81b4|119741|1784378845.815307013

  real backend bridge proof:
  locale: de_DE.UTF-8 de_DE.UTF-8
  missing result: null
  existing type: file
  existing size: 6
  existing mtimeMs finite: true
  existing mtimeMs has sub-ms field: true
  permission denied throws: true
  permission denied message contains stat failed: true
  used production sentinel: true
  used GNU stat protocol: true
  used python for stat metadata: false
  ```

This proves the production `createSandboxFsBridge().stat()` path:
1. Missing path returns `null` (not throwing by parsing English error text)
2. Existing file returns typed metadata with fractional epoch mtime (`%.Y`)
3. Permission denied still throws with `stat failed` message
4. Uses GNU stat `%f|%s|%.Y` protocol, not Python
5. Runs under non-English locale (`de_DE.UTF-8`)

target.title: fix(gmail): prevent duplicate watch renewals during stalls
target.body:
<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Gmail watch renewal could launch duplicate `gog gmail watch start` commands when a previous periodic renewal was still stalled. This affects both the gateway-managed watcher and `openclaw webhooks gmail run` when the configured renewal interval is shorter than the command's two-minute timeout.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each Gmail watcher lifecycle now admits only one periodic renewal at a time. Later timer ticks are coalesced until the active command settles, while existing retry timing, failure logging, configuration, and process lifecycle behavior remain unchanged.

## User Impact

Operators no longer get overlapping Gmail watch registration commands during slow or stalled renewals. Normal renewals continue on the next interval after the active command settles.

## Evidence

- Focused tests: `src/hooks/gmail-watcher.test.ts` and `src/hooks/gmail-ops.test.ts` — 2 files, 12 tests passed.
- Targeted formatting and lint checks passed for the four changed files.
- Production-lifecycle proof used the real `startGmailWatcher` scheduler and actual child processes. With `renewEveryMinutes: 1`, the first periodic renewal was held for 70 seconds; after 135 seconds exactly two watch-start calls were observed: the initial registration and one renewal. The minute-two tick did not launch a third command.

target.title: fix(boot-echo): keep echo guard chunking UTF-16 safe
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The boot echo guard's 80-char sliding-window chunking uses `.slice()` on UTF-16 code-unit boundaries, which can split surrogate pairs and produce misaligned chunks near emoji/CJK characters.

## Why This Change Was Made

Surrogate pairs split by raw code-unit slicing produce orphaned high/low surrogates in the chunk set, potentially causing echo matching to misalign near supplementary-plane characters.

## Code Change

The original `sliceUtf16SafeMinLen` retried only +1 extra character when `sliceUtf16Safe` trimmed the end for a surrogate pair. But `sliceUtf16Safe` can trim up to 1 char from the start (low-surrogate skip) and up to 1 from the end (high-surrogate skip), so the range may need extending by up to 2 to guarantee the minimum window length. The fix retries up to +2.

## User Impact

Users whose prompts contain emoji or CJK characters near an echo-match boundary may see incorrect echo detection behavior.

## Evidence

```
$ script -q -c "node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/boot-echo-guard.test.ts"

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  6 passed (6)
```

target.title: fix(scripts): bound check-workflows subprocesses
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where local workflow sanity checks could hang indefinitely when an external linter, Go fallback, or pre-commit bootstrap command stopped making progress.

## Why This Change Was Made

`scripts/check-workflows.mjs` now applies a fixed five-minute timeout to each subprocess it launches, escalates non-cooperative children, and reports which command timed out. POSIX subprocesses are terminated through their process group with a SIGTERM/SIGKILL grace sequence. Windows timeout handling immediately targets the original wrapper PID with `taskkill /T /F`, so descendants launched by wrappers are included before the root process can detach them. The timeout is intentionally not configurable, avoiding a new supported environment contract.

## User Impact

Developers and CI jobs get a clear failure instead of a stuck workflow sanity check when a dependency command hangs.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/check-workflows.test.ts`
- `pnpm format:check --no-error-on-unmatched-pattern -- scripts/check-workflows.mjs scripts/check-workflows.d.mts test/scripts/check-workflows.test.ts`
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.scripts.json scripts/check-workflows.mjs`
- `node scripts/check-script-declarations.mjs`
- `git diff --check`
- Focused coverage in `test/scripts/check-workflows.test.ts` verifies timeout escalation plans `taskkill /pid <pid> /T /F` before any root `SIGTERM`. The POSIX entrypoint fixture uses a Node preload hook to shorten only the fixed five-minute timer inside the test process; production code has no timeout override.
- A real `windows-2025` entrypoint run passed in [Windows proof run 29645563062](https://github.com/sunlit-deng/openclaw/actions/runs/29645563062):

```text
windows_entrypoint_status=1
windows_entrypoint_timeout_diagnostic=true
windows_entrypoint_wrapper_alive=false
windows_entrypoint_descendant_alive=false
```

- Real POSIX entrypoint proof with an `actionlint` fixture that ignores `SIGTERM`:

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/check-workflows.test.ts
result: 10 passed, 1 skipped on macOS
entrypoint fixture: actionlint --version succeeds; the workflow scan ignores SIGTERM
entrypoint status: 1
stderr: [check-workflows] timed out after 300000ms: actionlint .github/workflows/android-release.yml ... .github/workflows/workflow-sanity.yml
```

<details>
<summary>proof-check-workflows-timeout.sh</summary>

```sh
#!/bin/sh
set -eu

node_bin="$(command -v node)"
proof_dir="$(mktemp -d)"
mkdir -p "$proof_dir/bin"

cat > "$proof_dir/shorten-command-timeout.mjs" <<'JS'
const nativeSetTimeout = globalThis.setTimeout;
globalThis.setTimeout = (callback, delay, ...args) =>
  nativeSetTimeout(callback, delay === 300_000 ? 500 : delay, ...args);
JS
hook_url="$("$node_bin" -e 'console.log(require("node:url").pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]).href)' "$proof_dir/shorten-command-timeout.mjs")"

cat > "$proof_dir/bin/actionlint" <<SH
#!$node_bin
if (process.argv[2] === "--version") process.exit(0);
process.on("SIGTERM", () => {});
setInterval(() => {}, 10_000);
SH
chmod +x "$proof_dir/bin/actionlint"

set +e
NODE_OPTIONS="--import=$hook_url" PATH="$proof_dir/bin:$PATH" "$node_bin" scripts/check-workflows.mjs >"$proof_dir/stdout.txt" 2>"$proof_dir/stderr.txt"
exit_code=$?
set -e

printf 'entrypoint: node scripts/check-workflows.mjs\n'
printf 'fixture: actionlint --version succeeds; actionlint workflow scan ignores SIGTERM\n'
printf 'status: %s\n' "$exit_code"
printf 'stderr: %s\n' "$(tr '\n' ' ' < "$proof_dir/stderr.txt" | sed 's/  */ /g')"
```

</details>

target.title: fix(ai): keep OpenAI tool call id truncation UTF-16 safe
target.body:
<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where OpenAI-provider tool-call conversations could send invalid Unicode in outbound `tool_call_id` values when an oversized ID contained a UTF-16 surrogate pair straddling the 40-code-unit truncation boundary.

## Why This Change Was Made

`normalizeToolCallId` truncated with `id.slice(0, 40)`. `String.prototype.slice` cuts UTF-16 code units, so a surrogate pair such as 🐱 (`\uD83D\uDC31`) at positions 39–40 left an unpaired high surrogate on the wire.

The fix switches that OpenAI branch to the existing repo helper `truncateUtf16Safe` from `@openclaw/normalization-core/utf16-slice` (same helper used by sibling UTF-16 surfaces). Non-OpenAI provider paths and the pipe-separated ID branch are unchanged.

Collision check: searched open PRs; no same-file or same-problem open PR was found.

## User Impact

- Multi-model `openai` provider tool-call conversations keep valid Unicode in truncated IDs
- IDs without a surrogate pair at the 40-unit boundary behave as before
- Non-OpenAI provider truncation paths are unchanged

## Evidence

Exact head: `ceef3b13cf17a3f887ede49ad704ab705661dc71`

Focused suites:

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/ai/src/providers/openai-completions.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  47 passed (47)

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/ai/src/providers/openai-completions.tool-call-id-utf16-loopback.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed (1)
```

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior or issue addressed: Oversized OpenAI tool-call IDs whose surrogate pair crosses the 40 UTF-16 code-unit limit no longer leave an unpaired high surrogate in the outbound `/v1/chat/completions` request body.
- Real environment tested: Windows 10 + Node v24.17.0 + local checkout at `ceef3b13cf17a3f887ede49ad704ab705661dc71`.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:
  ```bash
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/ai/src/providers/openai-completions.tool-call-id-utf16-loopback.test.ts
  ```
  Colocated loopback test (same pattern as `anthropic.fetch-loopback.test.ts` / `mistral.bounded-stream.test.ts`): starts a redacted `127.0.0.1` OpenAI-compatible HTTP server, drives production `streamOpenAICompletions` through the real OpenAI SDK (no `vi.mock("openai")`), and asserts the `tool_call_id` bytes received on `POST /v1/chat/completions`.
- Evidence after fix:
  ```text
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
       Tests  1 passed (1)

  Wire assertions (production path → loopback):
  - request_method=POST
  - request_path includes /chat/completions
  - stop_reason=stop
  - raw String.prototype.slice(0,40) baseline: trailing_high_surrogate=true, last_code_unit=0xd83d
  - received_tool_call_id length=39 ASCII prefix, trailing_high_surrogate=false
  - received id differs from broken raw slice
  ```
  Earlier equivalent live loopback run (same production path, before relocating the harness into the colocated test) printed:
  ```text
  AFTER fix (bytes received by loopback OpenAI-compatible endpoint):
  {
    "request_method": "POST",
    "request_path": "/v1/chat/completions",
    "stop_reason": "stop",
    "received_tool_call_id": "aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa",
    "analysis": {
      "length": 39,
      "last_code_unit": "0x61",
      "trailing_high_surrogate": false,
      "prefix_preserved": true
    }
  }
  ALL PROOF ASSERTIONS: 9 passed, 0 failed
  ```
- Observed result after fix: The production openai-completions runtime sends a 39-code-unit ASCII `tool_call_id` to the loopback endpoint with no trailing high surrogate. The broken `slice(0, 40)` baseline still shows unpaired `0xd83d`.
- What was not tested: Live paid OpenAI API round-trip with a real API key; non-OpenAI provider truncation branches (intentionally unchanged).
